name: Aadland For Colorado
subject: Water in the West
body:
The lifeblood of our state
| | | | | Volume 40 | May 4, 2022
---
|
---
| A word from Erik
---
| | |
---|---
|
Water is the lifeblood of our state, and a particularly hard-hitting concern for many Coloradans and fellow Americans in the southwest, especially those in the agricultural sectors.

The federal government, guided by Representatives who know the issues and can educate fellow members as to how to protect this resource, must ensure our precious resources meet the needs of our growing population. With my significant experience in the energy sector, and my awareness regarding these issues, I would be privileged to serve on Congress's Natural Resources Committee, where I may work to solve many of these most pressing issues.
| |
---|---
|
The Colorado River is a vital national treasure and resource. Millions of Coloradans are dependent on it for drinking water, irrigation for ranches and farms, and hydro-electric power. We also know that the current system is nearing crisis.

With significant population growth in many western states, combined with droughts and poor management of resources nationwide, we must act now to develop policies well into the future that ensure the availability of this critical resource.
| |
---|---
|
Since a significant number of states are affected by water shortages, some intervention by legislation may prove necessary. I will continue to protect Colorado from those who wish to renege on the Interstate Compact. We need real cooperation among the states which will yield far better results than actions by activist courts. The more cooperation we can generate, the fewer harmful lawsuits we will see.
Ultimately, private innovation is necessary for problem-solving related to water issues, and most pressing is the need to address the western water supply that is dwindling, even as demand continues to grow.
Increasing the efficiency of urban usage as well as recycling efforts even as we decrease wastewater are important first steps. Sometimes, we must look to other parts of the world for solutions. Israel, for example, recycles 80 percent of its water supply by ingeniously treating wastewater, which accounts for nearly half of the water used for their agriculture.
---
| |
---|---
|
Desalination plants on the west coast, such as that in Santa Barbara, California, offer another potential answer. This method of creating fresh water is expensive, but all methods have inherent costs.

State by state water management is necessary. Taking less water from existing sources may stave off levels that make pumping out water very difficult or impossible given current technology.

Water storage mechanisms are important ways to build up water supplies during years of higher-than-average precipitation. One example of this is the Blue Mesa Reservoir in western Colorado. Voluntary flow programs, such as the Arkansas River Voluntary Flow Management Agreement, also offer hope in ensuring water is available when it is most desperately needed.

Together, we can incentivize ingenuity to solve these challenging problems, without increasing regulations or government involvement.

Finding solutions to water issues in our western states is a national issue with significant consequences, if we fail to adequately address it. I will fight for Colorado and for our fellow Americans to do what is right for all of us.
|

---|---
|
More Walkabouts!
Last Saturday morning, Erik and Team Aadland walked neighborhoods in Golden, talking to folks about their concerns. The reception was very positive and our neighbors in Golden are solidly behind Erik to be our Representative in DC.

Saturday evening, GOP organizations in Fremont and Park counties each hosted their Lincoln Day Dinner.

At the Fremont County event, Erik spoke to the crowd of around 200 about his leadership experience and strength of character. The enthusiastic applause confirmed that the attendees believe, it is critical that we send these characteristics to DC in our representation. Erik received the noticeably strongest approval from the audience. Other campaigns were represented including Greg Lopez for Governor, who was very well received.

Erik was not able to attend the dinner in Park County due to prior commitment on the same night in Fremont County. Our Area Coordinator Tim LeBlanc spoke on Erik's behalf and gave an ardent and powerful three-minute capsulation of what Erik's candidacy means. Tim's words were received with focus from the audience and enthusiastic applause at the end.

subject: Making a mockery of our border
body:
Peter,

Because Rep. Tony Gonzales is the most vulnerable member of Congress, he invited Republican Minority Leader Kevin McCarthy and a delegation to make a mockery of a serious situation plus the men and women who work hard everyday to address the multitude of challenges at the border.

To them it’s a photo op. So, instead, John wanted to start creating real solutions.

In partnership with the Maverick County Democrats, community leaders, and local stakeholders — John hosted a "Our Border, Our Solutions" round table in Eagle Pass, TX about the border and the lifting of Title 42.

Title 42 is a pandemic-era health order used by federal immigration officials to expel migrants — including asylum-seekers — at the U.S.-Mexico border.

John Lira wants to ensure that we are working together to make decisions about this as important as this — and that he can take solutions to Washington to protect the people and our border.

This is the kind of representative we deserve — someone who prioritizes creating solutions for the people over photo ops. If you also believe our representative should work for the people, make a donation right now to fund our work on the ground to elect John Lira.

Donate » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lira-em-20220504?refcode=em20220504]

This is what it looks like when a leader works together with a community.

This is what it looks like when a leader hears the people out, and includes their voices in decision and policy making.

This is what it looks like for a leader to jump in and start making real change for a district.

Unfortunately, our current Rep. Tony Gonzales is doing the very opposite of all of this — doing little to nothing to solve the serious immigration and border issues we are facing.

It’s time for a change — and a leader the people deserve. Make a donation right now to fund our fight to replace Tony Gonzales with that leader, John Lira.

Thank you for your support,
Paul De La Peña

Last night, Politico reported the Supreme Court has voted to strike down the landmark Roe v. Wade decision. [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44923333/343691168/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MGJlMGI4ZC1kZGNiLWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MGelPN0hg_5dAIQGIydkCOmtAG5lc8hDx-VNP1xo8yk=&emci=70b4a2e3-b0cb-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&emdi=40be0b8d-ddcb-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&ceid=15820338)

Peter,

Earlier this week, a report from _Politico_ said that in a draft opinion, the Supreme Court voted to overturn _Roe v. Wade_.

First, let me make it clear: until a final ruling is made public, abortion remains legal in our country. **However, if this draft opinion is issued, it marks a massive step backward for reproductive rights.**

Thirteen states already have "trigger bans" in place which will make abortion illegal overnight if Roe is overturned, and several more have passed extreme restrictions. Women in more than half of states will lose the freedom to make the most profoundly impactful healthcare decision of their lives -- when and whether to have a child.

Peter, this feels like a punch in the gut. As a doctor, I know that deeply personal reproductive decisions should be between patient and doctor. The government should never be in charge of these decisions. Overturning _Roe_ will not stop abortions. It will push them later into pregnancy and make them less safe. And for those forced to carry a pregnancy they did not choose, that pregnancy carries real risks to their health. Consider that the maternal mortality rate in the United States is more than double the rate in Canada.

Last year, with my pro-choice colleagues in the House, I helped pass the Women's Health Protection Act to codify _Roe v. Wade_ and block states from enacting medically unjustified barriers to accessing abortion care. As the only pro-choice woman doctor in the House, I will continue to work to ensure that we protect this fundamental right for every woman, no matter where she lives -- but I need your help.

Thank you,

Kim

Friend,
---
Naturally, the Left is panicking now that Elon Musk has purchased Twitter in a move to reform the platform and restore free speech.
---
As someone who was censored by Facebook in a clear attempt to undermine my campaign’s fundraising immediately after winning the Republican nomination, this acquisition from Musk couldn’t have come any sooner.
---
_But of course, liberal talking heads are crying foul, claiming Musk could censor any candidate he wishes...**as if Twitter didn’t do exactly that to President Trump.**_
---

name: Laura Loomer
subject: I’ve qualified for the ballot!
body:
This is very exciting, and I'm very proud of my campaign staff and volunteers, because qualifying via petition signatures is a huge accomplished, and no easy feat!
| | | [](https://libersend.lauraloomerforcongress.com/l/jaHkxHkvgw3mMH3vyc0Hsw/1hLBSM7hYxWcXBzCw8IWKg/GkZYdW8zo8IInx763yP7jdxQ)
Patriot,

[](https://libersend.lauraloomerforcongress.com/l/jaHkxHkvgw3mMH3vyc0Hsw/1hLBSM7hYxWcXBzCw8IWKg/GkZYdW8zo8IInx763yP7jdxQ)After months of hard work and grassroots campaigning on the ground, I submitted thousands of petitions to put my name on the ballot as a Republican Candidate for Congress in Florida's 11th Congressional District!

This is very exciting, and I'm extremely proud of my campaign staff and volunteers, because qualifying via petition signatures is a huge accomplishment, **and no easy feat!**

On top of that, we submitted more signatures than my RINO opponent, Do-Nothing Daniel Webster, who collected petitions by paying to send them in the mail! In comparison, my campaign team and I can say that we actually spoke directly to every single one of the voters who signed our petitions. **Daniel Webster will never be able to say the same!**

While I could have paid a filing fee of $10,400 to get on the ballot, it was really important to me to prove that I have grassroots support for my campaign. Also, it was a great opportunity to meet voters in my district!

But, it took a toll on our campaign coffers and volunteer resources. We had to drive thousands of miles over these last few months, and we had to pay $.10 per petition to have them verified. **That 's a lot of gas money and travel reimbursements.**

[Will you chip in to help replenish our campaign account?](https://libersend.lauraloomerforcongress.com/l/jaHkxHkvgw3mMH3vyc0Hsw/1hLBSM7hYxWcXBzCw8IWKg/GkZYdW8zo8IInx763yP7jdxQ)

**We 're down to 111 days before the Republican Primary, and we can't miss a day campaigning and meeting voters.**

We have so much to do, and the costs are piling up. [Any amount you can donate today will be greatly appreciated!](https://libersend.lauraloomerforcongress.com/l/jaHkxHkvgw3mMH3vyc0Hsw/1hLBSM7hYxWcXBzCw8IWKg/GkZYdW8zo8IInx763yP7jdxQ)

Thanks again for all that you do!

Respectfully,

name: Team Padilla
subject: (bump) Protecting Roe
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Padilla for Senate
body:
We wanted to make sure you saw Alex’s note from yesterday
#

Hi there,
We wanted to make sure you saw Alex’s note yesterday about the leaked draft Supreme Court decision that’s poised to overturn _Roe v. Wade_.
Read Alex’s thoughts below, and then [**please split a donation between Planned Parenthood of California and NARAL Pro-Choice California. We’ve already helped them raise thousands of dollars to protect the right to choose, but there is a tough fight ahead and they could use your support.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ap-em-may22-ppnaral?refcode=em220504-1-30&t=1&refcode2=784_159979_xinuBa&akid=784%2E159979%2ExinuBa)
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ap-em-may22-ppnaral?refcode=em220504-1-30&t=2&refcode2=784_159979_xinuBa&akid=784%2E159979%2ExinuBa)**
\- Team Padilla

* * *
Hi there,
Like many of you, I was shocked by the news that the Supreme Court is poised to overturn Roe v. Wade and make it illegal to have an abortion in large swaths of this country.
I know it’s alarming, and we in the Congress must do everything we can to protect the right to choose — including eliminating the filibuster to pass legislation to that effect. But there are two important things to know right now:
1. This is just a _draft opinion_ , and as of today abortion is not illegal. But it does mean that a right-wing majority on the court is poised to destroy the right to an abortion — a right that has protected the health and safety of millions of American women for nearly 50 years.

2. Regardless of what happens with this opinion, _California will always protect the right to have an abortion._ I support Governor Newsom and the State Assembly’s plan to enshrine the right to an abortion in the state constitution, and my hope is that if the worst comes to pass and the Supreme Court does indeed strike down Roe, California will remain a safe haven for people seeking a safe abortion.

**But the urgency of this moment means we cannot afford to wait for this draft opinion to become law. We have got to act now and do what we can right away. That’s why today, I’m asking you to split a donation between the Planned Parenthood of California, and NARAL Pro-Choice California.**
[**Please split a donation between Planned Parenthood of California and NARAL Pro-Choice California. Every penny will go directly toward fighting to protect the right to choose, not a cent to my campaign.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ap-em-may22-ppnaral?refcode=em220504-1-30&t=3&refcode2=784_159979_xinuBa&akid=784%2E159979%2ExinuBa)
Thank you. I know this fight is only just getting started, and my team and I will be in touch with more soon.
\- Alex Padilla

Paid For By Alex Padilla for Senate
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com . Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you want to, you can [ unsubscribe here.](https://act.alex-padilla.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=4&akid=784%2E159979%2ExinuBa)

| | Peter, As the daughter of a union firefighter, I learned to stand up for workers at a young age. I carried my dad's lessons with me when I served in the state legislature, championing an increase in our minimum wage and paid sick days for all workers. And as Oregon's Labor Commissioner, I fight for workers every day to ensure that they are paid the wages and benefits they have earned and are owed under the law. Wage theft remains a serious problem, and it takes many forms. We see too many instances of workers being misclassified by their employer to avoid paying them correct wages and to dodge employer payroll tax responsibilities. When a worker is misclassified as an independent contractor, it means they don't have access to health insurance, workers comp or unemployment benefits. **A lot of political campaigns don't "technically" employ any staff – they classify their campaign workers as independent contractors.** I think that's just wrong, Peter. That's why I pay my campaign staff a living wage. They're on payroll and receive health insurance – and we pay our interns too, because nobody should have to work for free. clean_body: | | | Peter, As the daughter of a union firefighter, I learned to stand up for workers at a young age. I carried my dad's lessons with me when I served in the state legislature, championing an increase in our minimum wage and paid sick days for all workers. And as Oregon's Labor Commissioner, I fight for workers every day to ensure that they are paid the wages and benefits they have earned and are owed under the law. Wage theft remains a serious problem, and it takes many forms. We see too many instances of workers being misclassified by their employer to avoid paying them correct wages and to dodge employer payroll tax responsibilities. When a worker is misclassified as an independent contractor, it means they don't have access to health insurance, workers comp or unemployment benefits. A lot of political campaigns don't "technically" employ any staff – they classify their campaign workers as independent contractors. I think that's just wrong, Peter. That's why I pay my campaign staff a living wage. They're on payroll and receive health insurance – and we pay our interns too, because nobody should have to work for free. Words mean nothing without action. I don't just say I fight for workers — I lead by example and pay by example. That's what my dad taught me and I've lived these values every day of my life. And let's be clear about the choice that voters have in this election. My Republican opponent, Alek Skarlatos, worked for the Freedom Foundation - that's about as anti-worker as it gets. He's gaining steam and has raised almost $2 million in his effort to flip this district. body:
[https://als-totem.s3.amazonaws.com/core/spacer.gif] On Monday night, we got the news that the Supreme Court might overturn Roe V. Wade, jeopardizing the rights of millions of women here in Michigan over their own bodies and futures. [https://als-totem.s3.amazonaws.com/core/spacer.gif]
Jocelyn says it best: “The fight for democracy is the fight for freedom is the fight for choice.”
It shouldn’t shock you to learn that Kristina Karamo’s views on choice are just like the rest of her positions: at best, unhinged, and at worst, dangerous. She compared the pro-choice movement to Satanic worship and said the arguments in favor of it are akin to the arguments justifying slavery.
Read that again, friend, and understand the danger Karamo poses to our state. She’s just too extreme – and too focused on crazy conspiracy theories to deliver any kind of competent leadership.
We can’t let Kristina Karamo anywhere near this office. Donate to Jocelyn’s re-election campaign today, friend. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/benson-landing1?refcode=050422]
-Team Benson
---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Team Benson
Date: Tuesday, May 4, 2022 at 5:17 PM
Subject: We can't go back to 1931
To: Our friend

Friend, it’s all the fight. The fight for democracy is the fight for freedom is the fight for choice. And in Michigan, that’s a fight going back nearly a century.

In 1931, the state of Michigan passed a deeply unjust law criminalizing abortion in nearly every circumstance -- including for rape and incest.
If the U.S. Supreme Court overturns Roe v. Wade, millions of women here in Michigan lose nearly every right to their own bodies and futures -- and will be subject to a law that dates back nearly a century.

While it is possible the court's opinion will change in some way before it is final, we should not expect the ultimate decision to change. This is the cumulative effect of a 40-year assault on our rights by extremists on the far right. From the Federalist Society and law schools, to circuit courts and the three most recent appointees to the Supreme Court.

What is clear is that these extremists and their hand-picked judges will keep using states' rights as a shield to strip as many federal protections as possible from those who need them most. They will "return" these decisions to the states, where in many cases the deck is already stacked due to partisan gerrymandering, judicial appointments, and voter suppression. One of the arguments in the leaked opinion is that if a right "is not deeply rooted in the Nation’s history and traditions" (direct quote) then it should not be a right.

This apparent decision on Roe is far more ominous for that reason. It eliminates the right to privacy. It will probably also be used to overturn our rights to contraception and even marriage equality, and that's just for starters. It also sets the stage for a future opinion that voting itself is no longer a fundamental right, based on the court's opinion in this case. And while this sounds extreme, remember that this has been a long time coming. Each of these rights could be taken away in the next five to seven years.

In this new judicial climate, state and local elections will matter more than ever. And having fair, accurate elections takes on even more importance.
The preservation of every right we have left -- and clawing back what the extremists are able to take away via five unelected judges -- depends on whether we exercise the right to vote. And of course, if that vote is counted.

Supreme Court Justice Sotomayor has suggested that the Court would not survive the court of public opinion if it overturned Roe v. Wade. That the Court would no longer represent a distinct arm of our democracy and would instead be reading the Constitution as a political act.
Like I said: The fight for democracy is the fight for freedom is the fight for choice. It's -all- the fight.

Thank you for being with me -- and all the causes to protect our rights that you support.

One of the arguments in the leaked opinion is that if a right "is not deeply rooted in the Nation’s history and traditions" (direct quote) then it should not be a right. This apparent decision on Roe is far more ominous for that reason. It eliminates the right to privacy. It will probably also be used to overturn our rights to contraception and even marriage equality, and that's just for starters. It also sets the stage for a future opinion that voting itself is no longer a fundamental right, based on the court's opinion in this case. And while this sounds extreme, remember that this has been a long time coming. Each of these rights could be taken away in the next five to seven years. In this new judicial climate, state and local elections will matter more than ever. And having fair, accurate elections takes on even more importance. The preservation of every right we have left -- and clawing back what the extremists are able to take away via five unelected judges -- depends on whether we exercise the right to vote. And of course, if that vote is counted. Supreme Court Justice Sotomayor has suggested that the Court would not survive the court of public opinion if it overturned Roe v. Wade. That the Court would no longer represent a distinct arm of our democracy and would instead be reading the Constitution as a political act. Like I said: The fight for democracy is the fight for freedom is the fight for choice. It's -all- the fight. Thank you for being with me -- and all the causes to protect our rights that you support. The Supreme Court draft opinion that was leaked on Monday night is both shocking and disheartening. Overruling Roe v. Wade would pose a threat to the reproductive rights of thousands of people, specifically women of color and the working class.
The percentage of people who already lack proper access to reproductive healthcare is astoundingly high in the United States–and Black women are disproportionately at risk. The sexism, racism, and lack of substantial policy informing these statistics must be addressed, and that begins with the codification of Roe v. Wade. Hey there, Peter.
It may seem counterproductive to say this, but I hate fundraising. I hate that it's necessary for a political campaign and frankly loathe the idea of asking friends and strangers for their hard-earned money. It's a breath of fresh air when my fundraising team says, "let's give our supporters a break from emails and texts so folks don't get burned out." At our Monday meeting we kicked around ideas, and what days we should send out a message - my campaign manager even made a version of my logo with crossed light-sabers for today, May the Fourth to share on social media. We initially weren't planning to send out anything until the 5th, for Cinco de Mayo - and that wasn't for fundraising - it was going to be a celebration of the diverse cultures that have blended together to make America such a great country. And then the SCOTUS draft decision to overturn _Roe V Wade_ was leaked and all hell broke loose. Where do my opponents stand on this? Joe Kent has stated plainly that it isn't a woman's right to choose whether or not to have an abortion. Hyper-evangelical Heidi St John has been beating the "pro-life" drum for longer than she's had an audience. And true to form, the GOP incumbent, Jaime Herrera Beutler dodges the issue in public but her voting history and legislative record say it loud and clear - she's anti-choice. **All of these opponents are out-fundraising me. All of these opponents are polling behind me.** If I'm going to stay in the lead in this very winnable race for a Democrat in WA-03, we've got to get our fundraising hyper-charged immediately. March and April were our strongest fundraising months to date, so we've got a solid foundation to build from, we just can't slow down for even a day. Every donation I get funds voter outreach - so that I can get in touch with the voters of WA-03 and let them know that I want to serve them - all of them. Earlier this week we set a target to fund our yard and road sign budget. Name recognition is CRITICAL right now so we must get $10,000 into that fund as soon as possible. clean_body: | | Hey there, Peter. It may seem counterproductive to say this, but I hate fundraising. I hate that it's necessary for a political campaign and frankly loathe the idea of asking friends and strangers for their hard-earned money. It's a breath of fresh air when my fundraising team says, "let's give our supporters a break from emails and texts so folks don't get burned out." At our Monday meeting we kicked around ideas, and what days we should send out a message - my campaign manager even made a version of my logo with crossed light-sabers for today, May the Fourth to share on social media. We initially weren't planning to send out anything until the 5th, for Cinco de Mayo - and that wasn't for fundraising - it was going to be a celebration of the diverse cultures that have blended together to make America such a great country. And then the SCOTUS draft decision to overturn Roe V Wade was leaked and all hell broke loose. Where do my opponents stand on this? Joe Kent has stated plainly that it isn't a woman's right to choose whether or not to have an abortion. Hyper-evangelical Heidi St John has been beating the "pro-life" drum for longer than she's had an audience. And true to form, the GOP incumbent, Jaime Herrera Beutler dodges the issue in public but her voting history and legislative record say it loud and clear - she's anti-choice. All of these opponents are out-fundraising me. All of these opponents are polling behind me. If I'm going to stay in the lead in this very winnable race for a Democrat in WA-03, we've got to get our fundraising hyper-charged immediately. March and April were our strongest fundraising months to date, so we've got a solid foundation to build from, we just can't slow down for even a day. Every donation I get funds voter outreach - so that I can get in touch with the voters of WA-03 and let them know that I want to serve them - all of them. Earlier this week we set a target to fund our yard and road sign budget. Name recognition is CRITICAL right now so we must get $10,000 into that fund as soon as possible. We deserve a Governor who will STAND TALL for life! | | | [ ](https://GarrettForMichigan.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0473a6037c1be0f2423e4fd&id=2c30c2105b&e=fe4b890356)

| **Peter,**

The pro-life movement in America got some BIG news this week when it was leaked that [the Supreme Court had voted to overturn Roe v. Wade](https://GarrettForMichigan.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0473a6037c1be0f2423e4fd&id=78c3fb9257&e=fe4b890356) \- **_returning abortion law back to the states._**

As an unapologetically pro-life conservative, I am praying that the Supreme Court rules in favor of life - and the Constitution - by finally getting rid of Roe v. Wade.

**As expected, Democrats are furious.** Especially in Michigan - where Gretchen Whitmer and her cronies are running on a platform of unlimited _abortion-on-demand until birth._

Look at some of their responses 👇🏼
---
| [ ](https://GarrettForMichigan.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0473a6037c1be0f2423e4fd&id=026495ba71&e=fe4b890356)

| | Gretchen Whitmer - who destroyed our economy, crushed the education of millions of students, and created an unprecedented mental health crisis - has pledged to "fight like hell" to protect abortion in Michigan.

**How about protecting innocent babies and helping women in need chose life!**

And our beloved Attorney General Dana Nessel has already committed to _not enforcing Michigan law_ that protects the right to life - violating her oath of office and acting as a dictator.

At the congressional level, it gets even worse. Check out two Metro Detroit Democrats' temper tantrums:
---

[ ](https://GarrettForMichigan.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0473a6037c1be0f2423e4fd&id=f75e465ca6&e=fe4b890356)
---
| Make no mistake - _**Democrats are all in**_ on packing the Supreme Court with liberal Justices, trampling the Constitution and pushing a vile pro-abortion agenda.

Folks, you know my story - my mother was adopted, and if abortion was legal at the time, I may not be here today (I know some progressive leftists who wish that were the case 😂).

**I will always stand for those who cannot stand up for themselves.** And I will follow Michigan's law and work with the legislature - _unlike the terrible trio currently in Lansing!_

**Peter, if you believe Michigan deserves a proudly pro-life Governor, please pitch in a few bucks today.**

Click here to make a secure donation: [secure.winred.com/garrett-for-michigan/pro-life](https://GarrettForMichigan.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0473a6037c1be0f2423e4fd&id=f51cb633ba&e=fe4b890356)

Let me be clear – if this decision becomes final, this will be disastrous for Arizona. It will put the lives of Arizonans at risk and will send us back a hundred years. > Our path forward is clear – we MUST flip Arizona completely blue and elect pro-choice AZ Dems who will work to protect reproductive rights on a state level. Due to trigger laws and decades-old legislation, any decision to remove Roe could immediately mean the end to reproductive freedom in Arizona. If that doesn’t happen, you can be certain the Republicans currently in charge of the state legislature will find a way to pass new laws completely banning abortion – with no exceptions. But if we elect pro-choice Democrats, we can repeal these laws and codify protections. If the courts are going to follow the GOP down an extremist path and overturn decades of precedent, then we have to pass laws to make things right again. body:
The NRA is arguing in this case that people should be allowed to carry concealed guns anywhere.
#

Friends -
The same Supreme Court that appears ready to overturn _Roe v. Wade_ is also considering another case—and it’s one we think you need to know about, and prepare for.
The case is _New York State Rifle and Pistol Association v. Bruen_.
And in this case, NYSRPA, the NRA’s New York affiliate, is challenging the State of New York over its permit requirements for the concealed carry of firearms.
The NRA is arguing in this case that people should be allowed to carry concealed guns anywhere. Can you imagine the crowd in the middle of Times Square during NYC’s New Year’s Eve celebration if many of the revelers there were carrying hidden guns?
One of the _many_ reasons the Supreme Court’s abortion decision has us so troubled is because this court has made a dramatic rightward lurch and we need to prepare for this decision going the wrong direction on gun safety as well.
Courts have ruled over and over that commonsense gun safety measures do not infringe on the Second Amendment. But the Supreme Court’s conservative majority may side with the NRA’s extreme philosophy instead.
That makes many of the local fights we’re engaged in—and winning—even more important.
Now we can’t win these fights alone. They will take all of us coming together. The road will be long, it will be difficult, but public opinion is on our side.
If we continue to fight, we are going to win. And winning means saving lives. That is why we have to ask:

name: Gisele Barreto Fetterman
subject: I grew up in a country where abortion was illegal.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fetterman for PA
body:
Abortion is an essential component of health care.
#
Derek,
**I grew up in a country where abortion was illegal.**
It was *illegal* but still one of the top five leading causes of maternal deaths.
So please, know that when I say we can’t afford to return to a pro-_Roe_ society, _I really mean it._
Abortion is an essential component of health care. And just like all other forms of health care, abortion services must be safe, legal and accessible.
**In order to do that, Democrats need to step up and pass the Women’s Health Protection Act to finally codify _Roe_ into law – even if that means scrapping the filibuster. **
And any Democrat who refuses to abolish an archaic rule like the filibuster, especially when _Roe_ is on the line, is failing us.
**Derek, John will always vote like a Democrat.**
He will _always_ put the fights of the people first, including the fight for the right to choose. He hasn’t had to evolve or flip-flop on the issues. His views when he first ran for this seat in 2016 are the same ones he has today.
[**Derek, if you can, please consider making a donation towards John’s campaign today. As the 51st Democratic vote in the U.S. Senate, he will help abolish the filibuster once and for all, so we can codify Roe, pass crucial voting rights, and more.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220504-1?refcode=em20220504-5665&refcode2=5665_434096_oVJhnJ&akid=5665%2E434096%2EoVJhnJ)

These are tough times, and I know it can be hard to maintain high hopes. Know that my family + I are sending you love and light. ❤️
—Gisele

name: Patrick Leahy
subject: Backward in time
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Leahy for U
body:
Friend,

I, like so many Americans, am disturbed by the news that the Supreme Court may be poised to overturn Roe v. Wade.

We cannot allow a narrow partisan majority to send us backward in time. This politicization of the court to attack a woman's right to choose should alarm every single American.

As we witness the erosion of our judiciary in real time, it is more important than ever that we shore up our pro-choice defenses in Congress. That's why my PAC is rushing support to three reproductive health champions who are running to keep the Senate blue this fall.

Please, join me in chipping in $10 or more right now to be split between incumbent Senator Cortez Masto in Nevada, challenger Rep. Val Demings in Florida, and challenger Cheri Beasley in North Carolina?
https://links.e.leahyforvermont.

Roe v. Wade was a landmark decision, which has enshrined the right of any pregnant person to have autonomy over their bodies for almost fifty years.

As the Supreme Court threatens Americans' constitutional right to choose, we must fight to keep the Senate blue – to remain a crucial check to prevent progress from being rolled back.

My colleague Senator Cortez Masto believes, as I do, that the right to reproductive health care is fundamental. Meanwhile, her leading Republican opponent is endorsed by the anti-abortion group "National Right to Life."

Rep. Val Demings has spent her career fighting to protect the right to choose, including passing legislation in the House to codify Roe v. Wade into law. Now, she's running for Senate to unseat Marco Rubio, who has consistently worked to make accessing abortions harder.

And in North Carolina, former Chief Justice of the State Supreme Court Cheri Beasley is running to fill the open seat currently held by Republican Richard Burr. While her Republican opponents jockey to see who can put forth the most extreme positions on abortion, Beasley is clear: Abortion is a constitutional right.

These are three women and pro-choice champions we need in the Senate as the Supreme Court attacks the autonomy of women and all pregnant people. Will you join me in making a contribution of $10 or more today to be split between their campaigns?
https://links.e.leahyforvermont.

Thank you for taking action alongside me today.

Sincerely,

Patrick Leahy
U.S. Senator

name: Steven Olikara
subject: Fighting for dignity means fighting for women's rights
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Olikara for Senate
body:
Image of Olikara campaign logo with photo of Steven Olikara and link to campaign website:
[https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/NGP/NGP30/1/90801/images/OfS%20logo%20w%20headshot.png]
[https://www.stevenolikara.com]

Dear Peter,

Fighting for dignity means fighting for a woman’s right to protect herself and the freedom to control her body. In the wake of the Supreme Court’s stunning draft decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, today I was honored to join a powerful rally in Milwaukee for human rights.

Photo of a crowd, caption:
The crowd at today's rally in Milwaukee

If Roe is overturned, an 1849 law would likely go into effect in Wisconsin, criminalizing all abortions, except when a mother’s life is at risk. This measure is unacceptable, even to many conservatives.

In this divisive time, we need to build greater empathy in this conversation, humanizing the real stories behind reproductive health and family planning. As a U.S. Senator, I will convene these inclusive conversations across Wisconsin and widen support for dignity and healthcare in our country. I believe there are opportunities for higher ground with people across the political spectrum—from reducing unplanned pregnancies to ensuring kids are able to thrive. And, together we must uphold a fundamental principle in America: the Constitutional right to personal freedom, including women’s decisions about their bodies.

Let’s also look at how we got here. The way we fill the Supreme Court has lost all credibility. The lives of millions of people shouldn’t hinge on the personal health of Justices in their 80s. It’s time for Supreme Court term limits. I’m proud to be the only Wisconsin U.S. Senate candidate on either side of the aisle calling for this reform.

Join us in the fight for a different kind of politics and dignity for all.

Yours,
Steven

Dividing line

| | | Family, hard work and community. These are the things that have defined me as a person more than anything else and are the things that make New Hampshire a special place. Several local Salem community leaders became role models and mentors and got me involved with helping our community. With their encouragement, I ran for Salem Selectman and won. I ran for Town Moderator and won. Then I ran for State Representative and served for two terms from 1998-2002. I was elected to the State Senate in 2002 and was appointed to the Finance Committee. My experience running a business, meeting a payroll, and keeping a conservative budget helped prepare me for the challenges of crafting a balanced state budget. I quickly became known as one of the state’s leaders in budgeting and tax policy. I took a step back from politics in 2006. My daughter was starting her junior year in high school and Susan and I spent most of the next few years traveling to her field hockey and basketball games. We were her biggest fans. In 2010, I was reelected to the Senate. When I returned to the Finance Committee, I found the financial mess that the Democrats had put our state in. The state had an $800 million deficit. We quickly turned that around and put the state’s finances back on a sustainable path. For my work, colleagues gave me the greatest honor of my life — electing me the Senate President in 2013. In 2020, I led Republican efforts to retake the majority in the State Senate. New Hampshire was the only state in the country that was able to flip a blue state legislature to red and it was largely due to our strong fight against the Democrats’ proposed state income tax. Last year, we passed one of the most conservative and fiscally responsible budgets that New Hampshire has ever seen. It is balanced, cuts taxes for small businesses, provides more than $300 million in property tax relief, bans late-term abortions, and prohibits the use of discriminatory teaching in our schools. It puts New Hampshire on a path to long-term prosperity. The work ethic, commitment to family and sense of community that I learned at a young age have stuck with me as an adult and drive everything I do. I still wake up at 4am every morning to work at our business before going to Concord to do the people’s business. More often than not, I still take my first phone calls of the day while driving a tractor. Washington, D.C. has enough silver-spoon, Ivy League lawyers. I believe that I am a product of all the best parts of New Hampshire — the spirit of freedom, sense of volunteerism and responsibility of giving back to the community that has helped shape me into the person I am today. I want to bring New Hampshire to Washington and makes sure our voices are heard. I want to bring New Hampshire values to a place that needs them now more than ever. I want to work for you and I hope you will consider electing me to represent you in the U.S. Senate.

| |
---
| Dear Kansans,

Today I am announcing that I filed for re-election as your representative for the Big First District. Serving you in my first term has been one of the greatest honors of my life. I serve in Congress to advocate for our _conservative Kansas values_. I’m asking you to support my campaign so I can press on with that same mission. I’m proud to come from the Big First - the geographic center and pilot light of America - where the values that make America great are alive and well: faith, family, hard work, and loving your neighbor.

We need to get this country back on track. The Biden Administration is letting China run roughshod all over us, mortgaging our children's future with national debt, paying attention to the wrong things like vaccine mandates, and doing nothing to secure our southern border, stop inflation, or fix the supply chain. The radical left has created one disaster after another, which is why I’m asking for your support. I did not come to Congress to be a caretaker in the slow demise of America, I came to work to make it stronger.

I am pro-life, pro-second amendment, pro-ag, and pro-freedom. I stand against big government socialism and always will. In the past few weeks, I’ve been discussing some of the ways in which America is in crisis. In the coming weeks, I will be sharing with you about my hopes for America’s future, and what I plan to do to make those hopes become a reality.

God bless the First District, Kansas, and America.

Yours in the fight,

Tracey Mann

P.S. I will continue to stand for Kansas as we move forward, and I will do everything in my power to ensure that our kids have a bright future. | A MESSAGE FROM **TEAM BRNO**
---
| ,

Restoring trust and confidence in our elections should be our priority. There’s no doubt that 2020 revealed serious vulnerabilities in our election processes and fighting to ensure transparency and accountability is common-sense. However, the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors and County Recorder continue to throw stones at Attorney General Brnovich instead of working to address the serious issues identified in the interim report. We’re only asking that our elected officials take these matters seriously, but it seems they’d rather further divide our state and ignore Arizonans who are concerned about their vote.

Brnovich has been on the frontlines fighting to secure our elections long before 2020 and continues to be a steadfast advocate for election integrity. We are disappointed in MCBOS and the County Recorder for continuing to stoke the flames of division instead of addressing the real and urgent concerns of our election processes. Arizonans deserve accuracy of the process and confidence in the results, and Attorney General Brnovich has been working to deliver that.
---
| \- Team Brnovich
